rationale: These four parts span 82 to 250 mm and every one of their meshes is a designed export rather than a scan, so the screening windows below are sized to the storage precision of the vertices and not to a measurement error nobody made. dump_path is written relative to this directory and the runner resolves it: the emitter sections the dump host-side, and it re-hashes those bytes against the program's dump_sha256 before reading any of them. The rejection budget is zero because a constraint this program cannot place is a reconstruction it cannot claim.

section_tolerance_mm.rationale: a hundredth of a millimetre is below the smallest feature any of these four parts carries, and above the float32 quantization their vertices are stored at.

classify_tolerance_mm.rationale: the same window: a section point nearer than this to a fitted surface came from that surface and not from its neighbour.

profile_chain_tolerance_mm.rationale: two section tolerances, so a chain closes across tessellation jitter without bridging a gap that is really there.

snap_tolerance_deg.rationale: half a degree is below the fitted axis sigma these runs measured, so a snap reports an alignment the evidence already carries rather than inventing one.

snap_tolerance_mm.rationale: five hundredths of a millimetre over parts this size: two features that agree this closely agree.

constraint_displacement_tolerance_mm.rationale: a constraint that moves a sketch further than this changed the geometry instead of describing it, and must be rejected rather than applied.

constraint_rejection_budget.rationale: zero: a constraint this program cannot place is a reconstruction it cannot claim, and a benchmark that tolerated some would be measuring its own tolerance.

entity_match_tolerance_mm.rationale: the window for binding a built face back to the fitted region it came from, at the scale these parts are modelled to.

loop_material_consensus_fraction.rationale: a section loop's walls vote by length for which side of the loop the material is on, and on a designed export they should be unanimous. Five per cent is the room a blend crossing or a sliver triangle at a corner needs; beyond that the winding is not noisy, it is saying the section crossed a junction or a degenerate feature, which is a finding and not a tolerance to widen.

loop_attribution_min_fraction.rationale: how much of a loop's length may lie on triangles that cast no vote -- degenerate facets, and facets parallel to the section plane that bound material along the axis rather than across the loop -- before the loop's walls stop being evidence. The same five per cent as the consensus slack, for the same reason: these sections are taken at the mid-station precisely to be far from the caps, so a loop that grazes one there is a station problem rather than a mesh to make allowances for.

sketch_loop_budget.rationale: a runtime guard, not a solver limit, and measured as one. A live Fusion (2.0.23164) enumerated profiles correctly and built a healthy extrude for every sketch up to 192 disjoint loops -- profiles.count matched the loop count exactly and total area was exact at every step -- so nothing was found to break. What does grow is the cost of *drawing* the sketch through the API: 0.048 s at 8 loops, 1.46 s at 64, 14.3 s at 192, roughly quadratic. 64 is the corpus maximum (POD-B-BASE closes 51 loops in one slab) with headroom, at about a second and a half of drawing. Raise it if a part needs more and the wait is acceptable; the number is here so that a 200-loop sketch is a decision rather than a hang.
